At dusk, a plain guide to floor markings
This article helps
Companion Animal Travel Desk floor markings

Floor markings help you move through the pet lounge, relief areas, and boarding paths with less hesitation. Follow the signs as they appear on the floor, and keep your animal close and calm while you move. If your pet is sensitive to noise or crowds, pause in a clear spot and let the pace settle before you continue.

When you reach a marked waiting area, stay within the outlined space and keep leashes short. The markings are there to separate walking lanes from rest zones, so do not block the center of the path. If you are carrying a crate or carrier, place it only where the floor guide shows a waiting position. This keeps traffic steady for other travelers and for staff.

At the pet lounge, use the floor symbols to find seating, water access, and cleanup points. <<FACT F002>> Keep your belongings beside you and avoid crossing into service paths marked for staff use. If your animal needs a quieter approach, choose the edge of the lounge and give it a moment to adjust before moving again.

For relief areas, watch for the ground markers that lead from the terminal walkway to the entry point. <<FACT F017>> Enter only through the marked opening, then follow the return path when you are done. If your pet hesitates, do not pull or rush; a steady voice and a slow step are usually enough.

If you need help with a marked route, speak with the nearest staff member and follow the calm stepwise review that is used for escalations. The team will look at the situation, the animal's comfort, and any special care notes before giving the next instruction. Care plans account for species, temperament, and comfort, so tell staff what your pet needs in plain terms.

If the markings seem faded, crowded, or blocked, report it at once so the route can be checked. For more help, contact the Companion Animal Travel Desk at Aurelia Skyways.
